To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the discriminant features are more effective than the principal components for image retrieval.
the discriminant eigenfeatures are more effective than the principal component features for view based object retrieval.
the discriminant eigenfeatures are superior to PCA in terms of retrieval effectiveness and computational complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) How to select the most discriminant features from the training set for image retrieval; (2) How to use the selected features in a retrieval system; (3) How to use them to retrieve images from a database.
the development of a new image retrieval method that is based on the use of discriminant features.
developing a method of image retrieval from a database of real world objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is superior to the principal component analysis in terms of both the classification accuracy and retrieval speed.
the discriminant eigenfeatures are superior to the principal component analysis features for view based object class recognition and retrieval.
the discriminant features outperform the principal component features in terms of the average precision of the top 1000 retrieved images, and the precision-recall curve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
discriminant analysis outperforms PCA in most cases.
the use of discriminant features for image retrieval can be very effective.
the discriminant eigenfeatures are more effective for image retrieval, and that the discriminant analysis is more suitable for image retrieval than the principal component analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most discriminating features can be used for view based object class retrieval.
the use of discriminant analysis is a powerful technique for feature selection and dimensionality reduction.

a linear discriminant projection is a powerful tool for feature selection, which can be used to select a small number of most discriminating features from a larger set of features, and that the resulting features can be used to perform effective image retrieval.
